messages:
nina: quick ping 1 Zenora asked to POC zenora-llm-65b:q5 in Dedicated. asks: is this variant in our catalog, KMS/EKM support, KV cache memory impact, and a POC pricing line item? can someone triage?

chris_l: who is the contact and expected workload shape?

nina: contact is sam@zenora.com. workload = mixed chat + long-document rerank; 6-10k contexts, lots of small concurrent requests.

maria_ops: i'll run a variant compatibility scan on a100-80 and check KV-cache behavior. starting job now.

presales-bot: scan kicked off: job=zen_scan_4501. checks: kernel-compat, kv-cache, tokenization, embedding-stability. ETA ~7m.

maria_ops: quick note: q5 generally reduces storage for model params but KV cache retained in fp16 may nudge memory. estimate +10% mem.

presales-bot: scan complete. job=zen_scan_4501. summary: kernel compatible, KV-cache overhead +9.8%, embedding variance <0.2% tol, tokenization parity OK. report: https://s3.redwood.ai/presales/zen_scan_4501/report.html

chris_l: sounds non-blocking. what about EKM?

sec-bot: draft answer: "Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS providers. External KMS/HSM (EKM) integrations require ops coordination and a short validation window; we can provision per-customer dedicated key flow under enterprise onboarding."

finance-bot: for pricing: q5 runtime approx -14% compute vs fp16; expect infra delta from KV cache +9%, and +one-time EKM integration fee if requested. i'll draft a POC quote for nina to send.

nina: great, i'll email sam with the report link and timelines: ops validation 1-3 business days, quote by tomorrow EOD. assigning: maria = ops validation, chris = tech follow-up, finance-bot = quote.

maria_ops: if they want parity 100% we can land a small tokenization patch but we shouldn't need it for the POC.

nina: thanks everyone. will reopen if Zenora requests deeper perf numbers."
